events.credibility_reason: 283-page computer-algebra-assisted argument with the hard chattering case excluded by a Poincare recurrence map; Kuperberg reportedly said 'they didn't really cross the finish line'; no peer review or journal acceptance found after 29 months. No specific error identified.

why: The statement asserts one specific thing: the smoothed octagon minimises maximum packing density. The only post-snapshot event, Hales–Vajjha 2024, proves (as claimed) that every minimiser is some smoothed polygon. That is a necessary consequence of the conjecture and narrows the candidate class, but it settles no restriction of the statement (no class, range or named part on which octagon-minimality is decided) and moves no quantity; the authors themselves say Reinhardt remains open. I scored it none rather than case; the competing reading (case, as a reduction of the candidate class) was weighed and rejected because the statement names no 'minimiser is a smoothed polygon' sub-claim. Cohn's reported confidence is second-hand and not a working-through, so unreviewed. Pre-snapshot: Ennola/Tammela is a bound on the minimal density; Nazarov's local minimality is a weaker form (variant); Kallus is a neighbouring question; Hales 2011/2017 and Vajjha 2022 are reductions/programmes (none). No AI system is credited anywhere.
doubts: The Hales–Vajjha scope call (none vs case) is the close one. The book's acknowledgements were not read, so the absence of AI rests on the abstract, introduction and early chapters. Ennola/Tammela and Nazarov are known only from secondary citations; 'digested' for them rests on journal publication as cited.
